name: scorm-mcp-server
description: Turn a self-contained HTML file, a Claude Design (.dc) bundle OR a mobile-learning platform content export (Excel templates + media) into a SCORM package any LMS can import — SCORM 2004 4th Ed. or 1.2, assets embedded for offline use, completion/progress/score and question-level (cmi.interactions) tracking injected, official ADL schemas bundled and validated. Also validates ANY existing SCORM zip and explains import failures.
long_description:
MCP server exposing three tools: `scorm_package`, `scorm_validate` and `scorm_selftest`.

Principle: WRAP, don't rewrite. Your HTML is preserved byte for byte; the tool only (1) embeds every asset as a data URI so the course runs with no network at all, (2) injects a small runtime that reports completion, progress, time spent and quiz score back to the LMS and resumes where the learner left off, and (3) generates the manifest and bundles the official ADL XSD schemas, validating against them.

SCORM 2004 4th Edition by default, or SCORM 1.2 for legacy LMSs — the injected runtime is adaptive and speaks whichever API the hosting platform exposes.

MIGRATION: a mobile-learning platform content export (Excel activity templates + media) is rebuilt into an interactive HTML course automatically — info/transition/flash cards, scored quizzes reporting cmi.score and per-question cmi.interactions, media embedded — then packaged. With batch mode, a whole catalogue migrates in one call.

Progress needs no preparation: if your HTML declares no milestone, they are auto-generated from the document structure. For finer control, mark steps with data-jalon / data-trigger, or call window.SCORM2004.reach() and .score() from your own code.

Also available outside Claude: `npx scorm-mcp-server ui` opens a local drag-and-drop page, `pack` packages from the command line (with a --batch mode for whole course catalogues), and buildPackage() is a documented library API.

VALIDATION: `scorm_validate` checks any existing SCORM zip — made by ANY tool — and explains exactly why an LMS would reject it: manifest at the zip root (detects the classic "zipped the folder instead of its contents" mistake), launch chain, missing or case-mismatched files, and full XSD validation against the official ADL schemas.

Runs entirely on your machine: no account, no telemetry, no data collection. Validated end to end on SCORM Cloud (completion, success and score all reported). 325 automated checks. Try it online first: https://scormpackager.vercel.app

tools.name: scorm_package
tools.description: Package a self-contained HTML file, a folder, a .zip, a Claude Design .dc bundle or a mobile-learning platform content export (Excel templates + media) as a SCORM 2004 (or 1.2) course. Supports batch packaging of a whole directory.

tools.name: scorm_validate
tools.description: Validate an existing SCORM .zip (from any authoring tool): manifest at zip root, launch chain, missing/case-mismatched files, XSD conformance — with plain-language explanations of every failure.

tools.name: scorm_selftest
tools.description: No-argument diagnostic: packages a built-in constant HTML and reports version, duration and output path.

output_dir.title: Output folder for SCORM packages
output_dir.description: Where the generated .zip files are written (default: ~/scorm-packages).
